findings.title: Insufficient Token-to-User Binding in Reset Password Route
findings.description: The reset-password API route uses findFirst() to retrieve ANY user with a valid, non-expired token instead of finding the specific user whose token matches the provided token parameter. This allows potential token confusion or collision attacks.
findings.issue: Query does not validate that the returned user's token matches the token parameter sent in the request body. With multiple users having valid tokens, findFirst() could return the wrong user's record.
findings.consequence: Attacker could potentially reset another user's password by sending a valid token from a different user account.
findings.fix: Remove findFirst() approach entirely. Instead, store an additional index field (like tokenHash with a different algorithm for lookups) or include user identification in the token itself. Verify the plain token matches the user's stored token before allowing password reset.
